claims.text: The conventionally processed FeNiCrCoCu coating has a coarse-grained structure.
The conventionally processed coating has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
The conventionally processed coating exhibits limited oxide formation.
A controlled pre-annealing step can refine the FeNiCrCoCu coating to a nanocrystalline grain size without undesirable phase segregation.
Nanocrystalline refinement increases the grain-boundary density of the coating.
The increased grain-boundary density supports more uniform and continuous oxide formation.
Grain boundaries accelerate oxidation along their interfaces during high-temperature sliding.
Rapid and uniform oxidation produces a tribologically protective film.
The protective oxide film reduces friction.
The protective oxide film reduces wear.
Fine grains shift microscopic deformation from localized dislocation slip toward distributed grain-boundary-mediated deformation.
Distributed grain-boundary-mediated deformation reduces microcrack formation and localized damage.
At approximately 600°C, the pre-annealed nanocrystalline coating will have a lower wear rate than the conventionally processed coating.
At approximately 600°C, the pre-annealed coating will show more extensive grain-boundary sliding and less localized shear banding than the baseline coating.
Under the same high-temperature sliding conditions, the coarse-grained baseline coating forms less continuous oxide layers.
Under the same high-temperature sliding conditions, the coarse-grained baseline coating has a higher wear rate.
Under the same high-temperature sliding conditions, deformation in the coarse-grained baseline coating is more localized and dislocation-driven.
The predicted wear and deformation benefits occur only in a high-temperature regime near 600°C where oxidation kinetics are active.
At lower temperatures where oxidation is suppressed, nanocrystalline refinement may not improve wear resistance or deformation behavior.

contradictions.description: The conditions field describes the approximately 600°C regime as being compared with baseline room- or lower-temperature conditions, whereas the baseline and falsification experiment compare the two coating states under the same approximately 600°C conditions. This leaves the intended control comparison ambiguous.
